items.title: Warren Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 17, 2018
items.q: Max had chosen us from his observations and experience with us... we all had so much respect for Max Roach that we just let him lead everything.

ctx.x: Wow. You’ve worked with some memorable musicians and artists over the years. And I believe you said you were talking about Max Roach. And he had an ego you said.

Oh man, that was an education in itself. I mean here’s a person who had a variation from piano to quadruple forte, even emotionally. You know I mean he could be the most kindest, most loving person in the world, gentle. But there were times when you could © Fillius Jazz Archive -14-

see him gritting his teeth and chewing his jaws and you could see where something was about to implode and he could erupt. You know he and I, I mean I guess maybe I’m an amateur psychologist. I like to read people. And I usually can avoid problems by anticipating somebody’s emotions. But I remember a couple of times he and I got into shouting matches about something. And something in me would never let me back down. You know, and we wound up being able to get along really well with each other because of that. But…
